acceptance: The site-parity report shows 0 stale allowances on develop.
A decision is recorded on whether stale allowances fail the gate, and the gate or its docs match it.
context:
Seen in the site-parity job for #2669 (2026-10-05): 'summary: 0 missing path, 0 missing fragment, ... 36 stale allow'. The gate failure in that run was a separate docs-header focus bug, fixed in #2675.

Correction 2026-10-06: an earlier note on this item said production still rendered with Sphinx and blocked the item on astro-site-53-cutover. That was wrong; it relied on the cutover item's tracker status, which is stale. Production is Astro: benchbox.dev/docs/ is generated by Astro 7.3.5/Starlight, deploy/routes.yml has renderer: auto (#2685), and site-deploy run 37406123669 (2026-10-06T02:50Z) built every route with Astro from tag v0.4.2. The block and the need were removed.

Owner widened the scope (2026-10-06): correct all stale entries and re-audit every link-check exemption. Audit on develop d076a974d with a full site-parity build (Explorer, Astro, Sphinx) and a Sphinx linkcheck run:
- known-broken-links.json: 36 of 66 entries no longer broken in the Astro build (removed); 30 still match broken links.
- docs/linkcheck_ignore.txt: 4 patterns match no link (localhost, cloud2.influxdata.com, api.onehouse.ai, pypi.nvidia.com) and the BTS TranStats /ontime/ entry's stated 404 is gone (200); all 5 removed. Others kept: they cover hosts that reject or time out CI runners (not disprovable from a workstation); benchbox.dev/results/compare?ids= is test-pinned and needed by a drafted blog post. Sphinx linkcheck: 143 working, 16 redirected, 0 broken.
- expected-removals-*.json and allowed-differences.json: 110 patterns match nothing in the Sphinx-vs-Astro build diff but all match in the diff against the published Sphinx baseline (0 stale there), which is what they record; kept.
- release-known-broken/v0.4.1.json: applies only to a v0.4.1 redeploy; the tag is immutable, so it cannot go stale; kept.
- redirect-pages.json (4), added-paths.json (7), allowed-inventory-losses.json (2): every entry verified against the Astro build. Owner action: the 7 added-paths.json entries still say owner_approval "pending".

PR #2736 (branch fix/site-parity-prune-stale-known-broken, worktree ../BenchBox.wt-site-stale, head 8540b4eef): after it, site_inventory.py check on the same Astro inventory reports 0 broken internal links and 0 stale allowances; 94 related tests pass.

Acceptance 2 (fail or report stale allowances) is waiting on an owner decision; the recommendation is a --fail-on-stale flag used only by the site-parity job (not a required context), leaving the production deploy gate tolerant. Do not finish until that decision is recorded and, if chosen, implemented.
description: The site-parity report lists 36 "stale allowance" entries: links recorded as allowed breakage (missing paths on the blog index, missing fragments in several ADR, examples and API-reference pages) that are no longer broken. Stale entries hide nothing today, but they would silently re-allow those links if they broke again. Remove them from the allowed-differences inventory and decide whether a stale allowance should fail the gate instead of only being reported.
